#1862. 'Would be very difficult to stop' - Gary Lineker names the one thing Brighton need to become serious Premier League title challengers

The former England striker, turned broadcaster, was discussing Fabian Hürzeler's side on The Rest is Football podcast – following Albion’s disappointing 2-0 defeat at Hull City. A victory would have taken the high-flying Seagulls to within three points to leaders Arsenal.

Brighton produced some impressive football but were unable to find a way past an inspired opposition goalkeeper, in Konstantinos Tzolakis. Their failure to convert chances proved costly, with Oli McBurnie stealing the game with a late brace.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Despite the result, Lineker was left hugely impressed by what he saw from the Seagulls. He described Brighton as the ‘best team to watch in the league’ when it comes to the quality of football.

The former Tottenham and Barcelona striker said he believes the addition of a clinical centre-forward could make Albion a formidable proposition.

"If Brighton had a nine like Leicester had in Jamie Vardy, I think they would be serious title challengers," Lineker, 65, said.

"They create so many chances. They haven't got, or at least I've not seen, a real nine in there that sniffs out [goals]."

The former Match of the Day host acknowledged that the Seagulls had played some excellent football but could not find the finishing touch.

"I watched the Brighton game yesterday, and I still can't quite work out [how they didn’t score]," he said.

"Well, I can, because they missed too many chances, and the opposition's keeper was unbelievable, but they played some incredibly good football.

"They couldn't score, which is unusual because they've scored more goals than any other team in the league this season.

"Even though they lost 2-0, I was thinking, God, Brighton are good.

"I go back to the point but if they had someone like a Vardy, wow, they'd be very difficult to stop, I think."

Regardless, Lineker said he ‘definitely can see’ Brighton in the Champions League next season.

His fellow podcast pundit Micah Richards agreed with the assessment. But he also felt the result was particularly damaging to Brighton's ambitions.

The former Manchester City full-back suggested that, if the Seagulls were serious about making a push towards the top of the Premier League, winning at Hull was essential.

"I know it's ridiculous – and we're talking about jumping on the bandwagon and being reactionary – but I think for a real push, they had to win that game," he said.

However, Richards, 38, was equally complimentary about the football Hürzeler's team are producing.

"I think they play some of the best football in the Premier League – they create so many chances," he said.

He agreed that they ideally need to sign a prolific number nine. But he was keen to stress that the comments were not intended as criticism of Albion’s current forwards – including Georginio Rutter, who started the match at Hull, and Charalampos Kostoulas.

"It's no disrespect to Rutter, he's just not got the clinical edge of a world-class player," Richards explained.

Richards also highlighted the contribution of midfielder Yasin Ayari, particularly his ability to make late runs into the penalty area.

Alan Shearer was another to praise Brighton's performance, describing the quality of their football and the pace at which they moved the ball.

"Great football, some brilliant football. They were passing and moving at pace – superb," the all-time leading Premier League goalscorer said.

The Newcastle legend added: "It was just one of those days where the keeper had his day and nothing was going to go past him. You have that and you just move on.”

Shearer, 56, also felt the result should not overshadow the quality of Brighton's display.

"I think he [Hürzeler] will be disappointed with the result, but performance-wise, I thought they were brilliant,” he said.

Brighton were not the only team to receive praise, with Richards also highlighting Bournemouth's recent formidable form.

The podcast trio agreed that the quality across the Premier League is improving, with Richards arguing that teams outside the traditional 'big six' are becoming increasingly difficult opponents.

For Brighton, however, Lineker's message was clear. He believes Hürzeler has a side capable of playing some of the best football in the country, but adding a striker with the instincts and finishing ability of Vardy could make them a much more dangerous proposition.

#1861. Columbus Crew vs Inter Miami - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 25 Nov 2026 14:16, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 14:19

On Friday, the Columbus Crew can pull off what may become the biggest upset in MLS playoff history and eliminate Inter Miami in game two of that first-round series at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field.

Last weekend the Crew took game one by a 3-0 score, putting them in position to eliminate the reigning champions should they win this upcoming fixture.

Columbus had a lot of momentum heading into the playoffs, and that continued on Saturday as they took advantage of some sloppy Miami defending to take a surprising lead in this series.

Laurent Courtois has seen his side score three or more goals in four of their last five matches versus MLS opposition, while posting a clean sheet in three of those instances, making them an appealing option to choose on the UK betting sites

The Crew exposed gaps in the Miami squad, scoring on three of their five targeted efforts last weekend and putting the Herons on the ropes heading into game two.

This is only the second time they are up 1-0 since this best-of-three first-round format was introduced, with this team advancing past Atlanta United in three games on the only previous occasion in which they were in this position in 2023.

Only once since their 2015 MLS Cup final defeat versus the Portland Timbers have they lost a post-season match at home, with the New York Red Bulls blanking them 1-0 in game one of that opening round series in 2024.

Friday will mark the second time the Crew can eliminate Miami from a major competition in Columbus, after knocking them out of the 2024 Leagues Cup thanks to a 3-2 victory at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field in the round of 16.

For a team boasting so much experience and talent in the biggest club and international competitions, Inter Miami failed to keep their composure in numerous instances last weekend.

Saturday’s defeat was the joint-worst for the club in the post-season, though given everything that transpired, they could be looking much worse heading into this match.

Kily Gonzalez will be relieved to know that Lionel Messi is available, escaping with just a caution in game one after throwing the ball at Gonzalo Tapia, a moment some believed should have warranted a sending off for the Argentine.

Miami played a good portion of that match a man down, and have never won the second game in a best-of-three MLS playoff series.

The Herons have given up a combined six goals in their last two matches versus MLS opposition and have yet to beat an MLS club in a knockout fixture this season.

The reigning league champions have lost four of their five all-time playoff outings away from home, with their only triumph coming at FC Cincinnati in 2025 (4-0).

Due to a cruciate ligament tear, Wessam Abou Ali will not be available for Columbus in game two of this series.

Gonzalo Tapia netted twice in Miami, with Taha Habroune also scoring as Patrick Schulte made three stops for the clean sheet.

On the Miami side, Mateo Silvetti is dealing with a shoulder issue, Tadeo Allende still has a knee problem and Israel Boatwright is recovering from a cruciate ligament tear.

Gonzalo Lujan will be suspended following his red card in game one, while Sergio Reguilon, David Ayala and Cesar Abadia are all questionable with lower-body injuries.

Schulte; Farsi, Moreira, Zawadzki, Amundsen; Zaroury, Chambost, Habroune, Rodriguez, Tapia, Mendez

St. Clair; Fray, Casemiro, Micael, Falcon; De Paul, Bright, Segovia; Messi, Suarez, Berterame

While Miami have all they need to come back and win this series, they are far too rigid defensively and give away too many quality scoring opportunities, which is why we believe their season will end much earlier than most would have expected.

#1860. Alexander Isak starts to justify £125m price tag with double

There was a centre-forward who played for Newcastle a couple of years ago. Do you remember him? He was as quick as greased lightning, played on his instincts, had a shot like cannon and could come up with a finish for every situation.

Everyone wanted him, but Liverpool signed him for £125m in August 2025. His name was Alexander Isak but shortly after arriving on Merseyside, it was like he went missing, as the guy who played in red last season bore only a physical resemblance to the guy who had played in black-and-white.

If you had wondered what had happened to him, he reappeared at Portman Road. They say good things come to those who wait. Although nobody at Liverpool would have expected such a delay to see the real Isak, there were no complaints that his career at the club has finally taken off.

Taking the headlines from Bradley Barcola on a big night at Portman Road was going to take some doing, but Isak did just that with a double salvo in the opening nine minutes, a flurry so potent it was like a boxer charging out of their corner and seeing the first blows land flush on their opponent’s jaw.

Poor Ipswich. There is universal recognition that Liverpool are a team – and a club – in transition but they had four players in Isak, Florian Wirtz, Cody Gakpo and Victor Muñoz who had the potential to dismantle the hosts if they clicked and that is precisely what happened.

“With Alex, it is clear,” said Andoni Iraola. “If he is fit, if he is available, if he is in a good shape, he will produce the numbers. My demand with Alex will not be about the goals. It will be about other things so we can play well. And if we play well, we are in good positions. Then goals will come.”

So for all the noisy backing they received from the stands and for all the effort Gary O’Neil’s side put into a contest that TV companies had chosen to broadcast because there was a potential for drama, Isak blew a hole in Ipswich’s hull in the sixth minute and they were submerging from there on in.

A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA

How Isak, who had scored against Nottingham Forest last weekend, needed a night like this when he made a genuine difference. But the same was true, too, for Iraola. We live in an era where someone has to be in the eye of a storm and the Basque will know what comes with his new territory.

It had clearly irritated Iraola that Liverpool had gone behind four times in their opening two fixtures and during his pre-match media briefing, he effectively gave a sermon at one point on how slow starts, or giving the opposition a helping hand, would no longer be tolerated.

Quietly, Iraola is making his presence felt. The task he faces is significantly different than the one O’Neil is accomplishing – keeping Ipswich in the division against the odds – but Liverpool’s head coach is a man who knows his own mind and is not afraid to make decisions.

He had responded to criticism of his midfield at Newcastle on the opening weekend by dropping Ryan Gravenberch for the fixture with Forest and his response to scrutiny about his right-back seven days ago was to drop Jeremie Frimpong and bring in Ronald Araújo.

Iraola certainly picked the right team: Araújo, the loan capture from Barcelona, added stature to the back four and there was harmony in how they moved. The Uruguayan’s first instinct was to stay back and Liverpool looked better for it, even if O’Neil, incredibly, felt Ipswich had the better of things.

Emersonn, Ipswich’s Brazilian striker, did not see the ball in the opening exchanges and, by the time he did, Liverpool had zoomed into the distance to such an extent that you felt it was going to be impossible for them to peg their visitors back.

“I hate having to talk about good performances when you do not get points,” O’Neil declared to a room full of raised eyebrows and you can only assume his message was to ensure that morale in the dressing room was not drooping.

What damage was inflicted with Liverpool’s first significant attack. Gakpo, the subject of an £80m bid from Manchester City, was never going to allow transfer speculation to disrupt his focus and he nudged a perfect little ball into Isak’s path in the sixth minute to show his wellbeing.

The next move announced the return of Isak. One touch gave him an avenue to shoot, the next was a shot with his right foot that was so hard from 16 yards, on an angle, it bent the wrists of Kjell Scherpen as it howled into the net. Critics will feel Ipswich’s keeper should have done better.

Your first thought was to think of the first goal Isak scored in English football in September 2022, a similarly venomous drive, against Liverpool at Anfield. He oozed quality that evening, his pace and skill had Jürgen Klopp’s defenders persistently fretting and this is what he was doing again.

It was no coincidence that three minutes later, he came up with another wonderful goal. This one owed much to the beautiful pass Gakpo presented to him, an inch-perfect through ball with the outside of his right foot, but Isak still showed great poise to bamboozle Scherpen.

Inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm

“He owes me a few assists now!” chirped the selfless Gakpo.

A hat-trick could have arrived in the 32nd minute but Isak was a kneecap offside as he dispatched a pass from Wirtz and, perhaps, he will have been disappointed to have made way on the hour having not secured the match ball for his efforts.

Liverpool, too, will be frustrated that they did not made sure of three points before the time Isak made way for Barcola – what Alexis Mac Alliser was thinking when he fluffed an unmarked header from six yards, only he will know – but it was not a night to nitpick.

There will be easier assignments on the horizon for Ipswich, even though O’Neil insisted they more than held their own against world-class opponents. And you can say for sure there will be more goals and wins for Liverpool and Isak if they continue in this encouraging manner.

“I witnessed what a great coach he was at Bournemouth. He is not the sort of manager you are going to see making clever patterns in his box. He just does not see the risk. He will want to get the ball to the players who want to make a difference. Coaches do not show how good they are by how they play out from the back. The important thing is when you get it in the final third, you make things happen. That is what he will want to improve. He will want Alexander Isak when he has not got the ball to press. He will want the same of Florian Wirtz. The difficulty will come with Champions League football and not putting too many demands on his players. If he gets it right, he has got a wonderful squad to work with.”

"My demands will not be about the goals, my fights with him are about other stuff." Andoni Iraola speaking about Alexander Isak 🔊 pic.twitter.com/B4zUG2IGfS

“He has had good minutes, a good pass in a counter, a good couple of chances when he was going against the goalkeeper and we have not found him. We need to learn these movements because he will be there threatening in behind all the team. But he looks confident on the ball as always. He had not played any competitive minutes since the World Cup so we had to be a little bit more careful.”

"Yeah, that's nice" 😁Alexander Isak talks through his second goal vs Ipswich 🔍 pic.twitter.com/diG2xv50Bw

“We were waiting for the first win, and we were talking about starting the game well, which we have not done recently. And we did that with two goals. With a normal pre-season, I think we are starting to get the way we want to play, being offensive and attack the defence. We showed that today. We scored two and could have scored more.

“It was not easy. It was a long injury, a difficult season [last season] in general. I was thinking; I want to have a good World Cup firstly and then to start the season well, which I feel like I have done now. That season is kind of behind me, but it was not easy.”

Cody Gakpo was linked with both Tottenham and Manchester City during the transfer window but stayed at Liverpool and has been in good form in these first three games of the season. He has assisted all three of Alexander Isak’s goals so far.

4 - Cody Gakpo has been directly involved in four goals in the Premier League this season (1 goal, 3 assists). This century, only Mo Salah in 2024-25 has had more goal involvements through Liverpool's opening three games of a league campaign (6).Retained. pic.twitter.com/hGN0NpF5A3

“You have to believe in yourself and have the belief of the fans that you are the man when you come for that much money. He had a terrible injury last year, but you can hear the Liverpool fans. They absolutely love what they saw. Some of his skills, his movement. That comes from his goal last week and the confidence that brings. Fingers crossed he can carry this on.”

The Swede’s two early goals have earned Liverpool all three points at Portman Road and the travelling Liverpool fans are singing his name. Isak’s fellow teammates are pushing him towards the travelling fans to take their adulation as they belt out his name.

The final whistle goes at Portman Road and Andoni Iraola picks up his first win as Liverpool boss with a 2-0 victory thanks to Isak’s quickfire double inside the opening 10 minutes. Like they did two seasons ago, Liverpool win 2-0 at Portman Road.

Enciso has a late shot from the edge of the box but it goes wide of the far post.

McAteer shoots from range but there is not enough power to trouble Alisson, who makes the save down to his right.

A late change from Liverpool as Koumas replaces Wirtz.

Due to that VAR review for the Liverpool penalty that was not, there will probably be five or six added minutes.

Clarke’s shot from just outside the Liverpool penalty area takes a deflection off his teammate Diop and goes wide.

Davis is getting a fair bit of joy down Ipswich’s left and the ball has been on to him quite a few times. He is being afforded too much space by Liverpool to get crosses in.

Andoni Iraola is bringing on Nyoni for Mac Allister, who was on a booking.

Davis is found making a run in behind and his cross from the left side of the box is blocked by Araujo and goes behind for a corner. Lukic’s delivery is headed away at the front post by Gravenberch.

Double change for Ipswich as McAteer and Ouattara replace Fatawau and Palacios.

Barcola drives down Liverpool’s left and, as he approaches the Ipswich box, cuts onto his right and feeds it across to Gakpo, whose shot misses the target.

The ball comes to Flemming on the edge of the box and he tries to curl one into the far corner but it is an easy save for Alisson.

Barcola is nearly played in behind but Scherpen does really to get out of his goal quickly and gets to the ball first, just ahead of Barcola.

Davis and Ipswich can count themselves very, very lucky. It would have been a penalty but Szoboszlai was offside when the original ball was played. For the second time tonight, an offside call massively goes in Ipswich’s favour; one to deny Isak a hat-trick and now to deny Liverpool a penalty. A massive let-off for Ipswich.

Liverpool are demanding a penalty. Szoboszlai is played in behind and is constantly having his shirt pulled by Davis. Davis then appears to bring Szoboszlai down inside the box but the referee waves it away. Davis gets none of the ball and the referee is being sent to the screen...

Barcola’s first few touches in a Liverpool shirt are pretty good down the left. He is playing in his most natural position of wide left, with Gakpo now down the middle and Szoboszlai on the right.

Gary O’Neil is going to make a double change as Clarke and Flemming come on, with the latter making his debut. Maeda and Emersonn come off.

So, here comes from the £123m Frenchman as Barcola enters the fray for his Liverpool debut. Gravenberch also comes on. There will be no first Liverpool hat-trick for Isak as he heads off, as does Munoz.

Bradley Barcola comes on to make his Liverpool debut! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/PjO78nlcqj

Andoni Iraola must be ripping his air out with the lack of composure and control from his side since half-time. It is no wonder he is about to turn to his bench and a certain Frenchman.

Enciso is given far too much space to drive towards the Liverpool box before shooting but Alisson makes the save. Liverpool, despite being 2-0 up, have showed a real lack of composure since the break.

If trends are anything to go by, Bradley Barcola will be introduced in the next three or four minutes. Andoni Iraola likes to change things around the hour mark and if the Frenchman warms up anymore, he will nearly overheat.

Kerkez is the latest player into the book for a foul on Fatawu.

Fatawu receives it out on the right for Ipswich and cuts inside onto his preferred left foot before curling an effort towards the far post but it goes wide.

Jacquet takes a heavy touch from a high ball and ends up taking out Emersonn, which earns the Frenchman a booking.

Liverpool work it well down their left as Isak plays it into Gakpo, who drives towards the Ipswich box. He plays it across the face of the penalty area to Szboszblai, who flicks it first time into the path of Wirtz. The German’s effort takes a deflection and goes behind for a corner.

Szoboszlai’s outswinger finds a free Mac Allister at the front post but the Argentine’s header is straight at Scherpen. That was a good chance for Mac Allister.

We are back under way at Portman Road. No changes for either side at the break.

We have just seen replays of a possible penalty shout for Liverpool right at the end of the first half for a foul on Gakpo by Fatawu and it looked a decent shout.

Perhaps if Liverpool were playing a team with a bit more savvy, the 2-0 scoreline they currently protect would have been in jeopardy. Ipswich have put some nice moves together and had half chances but not enough to really turn the screw. Andoni Iraola, certainly, has been unhappy at times and it is becoming a trademark to see him spin around from the technical area in disgust when a ball has been squandered. In the main, though, he can be satisfied with this opening 45 minutes. Liverpool should be winning from here.

The first half is brought to an end at Portman Road and Isak’s quickfire double early in the half gives Liverpool a 2-0 lead at the break.

Wirtz feeds a lovely pass into the left channel to pick out the run of Isak into the Ipswich box but Diop comes in with a crucial challenge.

Two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Araujo slices a clearance out of play for an Ipswich corner. A real gift for the home side as Araujo was not under any real pressure.

Isak should head away at the near post but it comes to Mac Allister to clear away.

A chance for Wirtz as the ball falls to the German on the edge of the Ipswich box but his shot is saved by Scherpen down to his left.

Enciso is the first Ipswich player into the book tonight for delaying a restart.

Szoboszlai, for the third time in the half, shoots from range. Again, the Hungarian gets plenty of power on it but fortunately for Scherpen it is straight at him.

Enciso turns neatly not far outside the Liverpool box and then shoots but slices the shot a fair way wide.

Tommy Elphick, a member of Andoni Iraola’s coaching staff, is booked for his protestations. Liverpool are not happy with some of the fouls being given against them and then some that are not given for them, including a clear foul from Emersonn on Van Dijk that was not penalised.

Isak has the ball in the Ipswich net for the third time tonight and thinks he has his hat-trick but the offside flag goes up. It comes from a stunning piece of play from Wirtz down Liverpool’s left, taking up a pocket of space and taking the ball on the turn beautifully. He then spots Isak in space at the far post and picks him out perfectly, with Isak slotting home. However, the offside flag is up and replays prove he was just offside. Could Isak have timed his run just fractionally better and still reached the cross? Probably but it was very close.

Mac Allister receives a pass from Wirtz and, from just outside the box, decides to shoot but his effort goes just over. Scherpen did appear to have it covered anyway.

A crucial intervention from Araujo. Enciso drives down Ipswich’s right after Fatawu’s header, with Mac Allister tracking back. From the right side of the Liverpool box, Enciso’s deflected cross comes towards Maeda at the far post but Araujo makes an important clearance.

Moments later, Davis again meets a Fatawu cross at the far post but his header is off target.

Fatawu’s dangerous cross from the right all the way to the back post finds Davis, who heads back across goal. Emersonn takes a touch with his chest on the edge of the six-yard box before shooting but Jacquet is on hand to make a crucial block. Ipswich though do have their first corner of the game.

Lukic clips it in and Alisson should punch away with ease. However, the ball comes off Gakpo and, very fortunately for Alisson, the ball gets trapped between his own legs and he can gather. Alisson will be a relieved man.

Szoboszlai sends another powerful shot from range towards the goal and forces Scherpen into another decent save. Ipswich are not helping themselves at times by just giving the ball away inside their own half.

Szoboszlai comes close to adding a third for Liverpool. Fatawu inexplicably gives the ball away inside his own half before Mac Allister plays it forward to Szoboszlai, who takes just one touch before firing towards goal. Scherpen gets down well to his right to make the save.

And there he is. You have been waiting 12 months to see the Alexander Isak of Newcastle play for Liverpool but here he is, a confident, instinctive-finishing menace. His first goal was marvellous, his second was a work of art, given the pass from Cody Gakpo, and what a position Liverpool have put themselves in to get their first win under Andoni Iraola. And, while we are at it, Gakpo has made both Liverpool’s goals: what on earth were they doing thinking of selling him to Manchester City?

Isak, on his last trip to Portman Road, scored a hat-trick for Newcastle here in a 4-0 win back in December 2024. He already has two goals to his name tonight inside the opening quarter of an hour.

Emersonn misses from close range for Ipswich but the offside flag goes up against Greaves. It was a bad miss from Emersonn but Greaves, who had delivered the cross for Emersonn, was offside.

The first booking of the game goes the way of Mac Allister, who is booked slightly harshly for a foul on Enciso.

Moments later, Ipswich have their first effort of the game but Fatawu curls over from the edge of the box.

Another fine goal from Isak and Liverpool lead 2-0 not even 10 minutes into this game. It is Gakpo who assists again with a superb pass with the outside of his right foot from halfway into the left channel to pick out the run in behind of Isak. The Swede cuts inside Greaves onto his right before then chopping back onto his left. He then coolly slots home past Scherpen and Liverpool have the dream start.

Inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm

Liverpool take a deserved lead at Portman Road. Kerkez wins the ball back for Liverpool on halfway and the ball comes to Gakpo. The Dutchman drives forward and spots Isak in space to his right. Isak’s movement is very clever as he drifts off the defender into space. He takes a touch before smashing the ball past Scherpen at his near post. Should Scherpen have saved that? Possibly but Isak did hit that very hard. For the first time this season, Liverpool lead in a Premier League match.

A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA

Wirtz is penalised for a very soft foul on Enciso, who just threw his hands in the air after the slightest bits of contact. The referee Darren England was not initially going to give it but eventually does, giving Ipswich the chance to swing it in from the left into the Liverpool penalty area.

Fatawu swings it in with his left but Alisson punches away.

It has been all Liverpool in these early stages but have yet to have a shot. Ipswich have barely touched the ball thus far.

Liverpool win the first corner of the game as Davis is forced to put it behind after good work from Munoz down Liverpool’s right.

Szoboszlai’s outswinger is headed away from danger.

The third matchday of the new Premier League season kicks off at Portman Road as newly-promoted Ipswich host Liverpool.

Andoni Iraola has drawn his first two games in charge of Liverpool, both 2-2 stalemates against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest respectively. Liverpool secured a move for forward Bradley Barcola from PSG in the final few days on the window for a fee that could rise to £123m and the Frenchman is set to make his Liverpool debut tonight.

“We are very happy with Bradley,” Iraola said. “He was our priority; to sign a very good player in that position. He has come with the right mentality. I like that he wanted Liverpool a lot, he just wanted to come here. That is a good first sign. Being the player he is and the things he has won recently, he has come with the willingness to help us. I am very happy with him.

“He trained well with us, and if everything goes well in today’s [Thursday] training, he will definitely be available for tomorrow [tonight]. He has trained with us three times. He has not had minutes in pre-season but he has been training normally with the group. It is a decision we have to make. We have to consider that he has not had minutes in pre-season.”

Liverpool won both fixtures when Ipswich were last in the Premier League two seasons ago, including a 2-0 win on the opening weekend in Arne Slot’s first game in charge of Liverpool as they went on to win the Premier League that season.

Ipswich won their first home game on their return to the Premier League, beating Sunderland 2-1 on the opening weekend. However, they fell to a 5-2 defeat in their first away game at Manchester United. Over the course of the summer transfer window, Ipswich made a total of 14 signings and spent over £200m.

“What we can do is perform in a way that always gives us a real chance, which we have done so far,” Ipswich boss Gary O’Neil said. “We were in that game at Manchester United until a couple of moments took it away from us. We were in it, so that is what we need to do, we need to make sure that no matter who it is, whether it is Liverpool, Manchester United, Manchester City, when they come to Portman Road, we need to make sure we are right in the game to give ourselves opportunities. We will always be a threat; we have scored four goals in two games. That is really good for a promoted side. We look a goal threat, and we need to keep that going and that will be tested.”

#1859. Brighton chief Paul Barber explains next step for new £80m stadium at Falmer

Brighton and Hove Albion will begin consulting supporters and stakeholders on plans to build Europe's first purpose-built women's football stadium in the coming weeks.

Chief executive and deputy chairman Paul Barber confirmed the next stage in his programme notes ahead of Thursday night's Conference League fixture with Craiova. Barber stated a public consultation event will take place in the Terrace at the Amex Stadium on December 9.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Barber said: "In the coming weeks we will begin consulting with supporters and stakeholders on our plans for the first purpose-built stadium in Europe and home for Brighton and Hove Albion Women, with an event planned for December 9 from 2-8pm at the Terrace at the Amex.

"It's a hugely important project, not only for our club but for the future of the women's game across Sussex, and we will share more details of the event very soon."

The announcement represents a step towards delivering a permanent home for Albion Women, with the club having formally unveiled its stadium proposals in April.

The proposed 10,000-capacity ground will be built at Bennett's Field, adjacent to the American Express Stadium, and connected to the Amex by a new bridge walkway.

Brighton hope to open the stadium in time for the 2030-31 season, subject to planning permission from Brighton and Hove City Council and Lewes District Council.

The estimated cost of the project is between £75m and £80m, with owner Tony Bloom backing the significant investment.

The stadium is being designed specifically around the needs of female players and supporters, with bespoke changing rooms, recovery facilities and a matchday experience aimed at families and first-time visitors.

Brighton currently play the majority of their Women's Super League home fixtures at Crawley Town's Broadfield Stadium, although selected matches have been staged at the Amex.

The new development would provide the women's team with a permanent base in the city and form a major part of the club's long-term ambitions to grow women's and girls' football across Sussex.

#1856. Five Man United players who could leave in January as part of major Mauricio Pochettino clear-out

By Matt Law | 25 Nov 2026 14:30, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 14:32

Manchester United are expected to be active during the January transfer window, with the club potentially making three mid-season signings.

The Red Devils currently find themselves down in 19th spot in the Premier League table and facing what would be a stunning relegation from the top flight.

There could also be first-team departures in the winter market, as new head coach Mauricio Pochettino begins to shape the squad.

Here, Sports Mole looks at five players who could potentially leave Old Trafford when the January market opens for business.

Zirkzee was linked with a move away from Man United over the summer, but he was ultimately not allowed to depart due to the fact that the Red Devils were unable to sign a replacement.

Even with Benjamin Sesko out injured, Zirkzee has not started a single match this season, with each of his 11 appearances coming off the bench.

The Netherlands international has scored twice this season, but his overall record for Man United since arriving from Bologna in 2024 is 11 goals in 86 appearances.

It has been a struggle for the 25-year-old in English football, but he is not short of interest, and a return to Serie A in January is seen as a serious possibility at this stage.

Como and Napoli are the latest clubs to be linked with Zirkzee.

Mazraoui is reportedly attracting the attention of AC Milan ahead of the January market, with a mid-season departure for the Morocco international thought to be possible.

The 29-year-old has underperformed in his nine appearances for Man United this season and is not believed to be in the club's long-term plans.

Initially, the defender impressed after arriving from Bayern Munich, and he has now represented the Red Devils on 86 occasions in all competitions.

However, a switch in the January market could be on the cards, especially if Man United are able to boost their options at full-back in the winter window.

Heaven is reportedly open to the idea of leaving Man United during the winter market.

The 20-year-old has made eight appearances for the Red Devils this season, including five outings in the Premier League, but he was an unused substitute against Liverpool in the team's last match, which ended in a 4-0 defeat.

Man United are expected to bring in a new centre-back in January, and Heaven is said to be concerned over what that would mean for his playing time.

As a result, the Englishman is allegedly open to a winter loan move, while a permanent exit is not being ruled out depending on what offers arrive.

Heaven, who has a contract with Man United until the summer of 2029, has made 32 appearances for the club since arriving from Arsenal in February 2025.

Martinez's contract with Man United is due to expire at the end of the campaign, and there is no getting away from the fact that it has been a tough season for the Argentine.

A new deal for the 28-year-old is seen as highly unlikely given that he has openly criticised Man United chiefs, such as director of football Jason Wilcox, during the 2026-27 season.

Man United will be reluctant to lose the Argentina international on a free transfer, so it is possible that a sale in the January window could occur, depending on the offer.

Martinez has been one of the team's biggest under-performers this season, and it appears that his time at Old Trafford will come to an end at some stage in 2027.

Amass may yet be given the chance to prove himself to new Man United head coach Pochettino, but the defender's future looks to be away from Old Trafford.

The 19-year-old was heavily linked with a departure during the summer window, but he stayed at Man United past the deadline and has made two appearances this season, both in the Champions League.

Amass was not in the squad against Liverpool last time out, though, and Luke Shaw's return to fitness has pushed him further down the pecking order.

A number of Championship clubs are believed to be keen on the teenager, who only has a deal with the 20-time English champions until the end of the season.

#1854. Pulborough football club fears over future of social club as council explores replacement plans

The parish council said it has been ‘open and transparent’ throughout the process of ‘exploring options for the future of the Pulborough Sports & Social Club building.

It said the project ‘remains at an early stage’, and ‘no final decisions have been made’ regarding the detailed design or layout of any replacement facility.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The club's members say the building is about far more than somewhere to have a drink after a match – it is a place where children make friends, parents get to know one another and volunteers help keep village football going.

Matt Parry, who has been involved with Pulborough football for around 30 years as a player and now as a parent and youth coach, said the club had become an important part of family life.

He said the youth section had grown to six teams, with players competing in local leagues and cups against clubs from much larger towns.

Matt said the club tried to keep costs down so that children could take part without financial barriers, adding that friendships formed through football often extended beyond the pitch.

After matches, parents and players regularly head into the clubhouse, while events bring the different age groups together.

A special family fun day last weekend celebrated 128 years of the youth football club. Matt said parents came into the building after the matches to socialise and take part in a fundraising raffle.

“We would not have been able to do that without the building at all,” he said.

Tom Hayes, who helped establish the club's youth football provision, also stressed the importance of the social club's support.

The youth section began with just four players and has since grown to six teams. Tom said the social club had helped from the outset, providing equipment and supporting the teams with kit sponsorship and presentation events.

He believes losing the facilities would mean losing an important part of the experience for children and their families, particularly those who value having an affordable place to meet after playing.

Natalie Smiley, who has been the football club secretary for around 17 years and also chairs the social club, said the two organisations were closely connected.

She warned: “If the social club goes, the football club will go with it.”

Natalie said the club had expanded considerably during her time involved, with six youth teams now playing alongside the men's side.

She said the work was carried out by volunteers, who gave up their own time to organise matches, prepare pitches and keep the club running. The social club also provides a base for other activities, including darts, pool and snooker.

The family day on Sunday, November 22, brought teams, families and supporters together. Natalie estimated that more than 400 people attended, while a raffle raised nearly £400 for football club funds.

Oliver Last, clerk and responsible financial officer, issued a statement on behalf of the parish council.

He said the council’s aim was to modernise the facilities rather than remove them, describing the existing building as ageing and no longer meeting modern standards.

He said: “The council's objective is not to remove facilities from the village, but to improve and modernise them.”

The statement added that the building ‘no longer meets modern standards’ for accessibility, safeguarding, energy efficiency or flexible community use. The council had been exploring whether to ‘substantially renovate or replace it for a number of years’.

The current concept being considered is a new sports and community hub, which the council says would continue to support sport while offering facilities for wider community use.

It said early proposals included modern changing facilities, social and hospitality space overlooking the recreation ground, community rooms, a youth area, storage for sports clubs, and ‘flexible spaces that can support a range of activities and community projects’.

The council also sought to address concerns about the future of the bar and social facilities, stating: “The aspiration includes a café/bar and social space and is not currently being considered to be used as parish council offices.”

It said the plans had developed since earlier proposals, following more recent consultation about local needs.

“More recent community consultation indicated strong support for a modern hub that combines sports facilities with wider community services,” the statement read.

The council added that sports clubs and community areas were identified as the most important activities for the hub, while respondents also supported social areas, café facilities, youth provision, community events and support services.

The council said it recognised Pulborough Football Club's contribution to the village and wanted the new facility to improve, rather than reduce, sports provision.

“The intention of the project is to strengthen and enhance sports provision, not diminish it,” Mr Last said.

He added that the proposed hub would provide ‘improved sports facilities, modern changing accommodation and enhanced social spaces’ that can ‘continue to support clubs, players, families and spectators’.

During the transition from the existing building to a new facility, the council said it would provide temporary changing facilities.

These would include separate male and female changing rooms, toilets and showers.

The council said the football club and other long-term users had been identified as key stakeholders, and that it remained committed to ensuring future facilities met their needs.

The condition of the existing building is another point of disagreement.

Mr Parry said there had been uncertainty about the proposals for years, and questioned whether money earmarked for a new building could instead be used to improve the existing facilities.

He said the building was still being used by the community, despite problems including leaks, and questioned why it could not be repaired and given a new roof.

The council acknowledged that users and volunteers had contributed to improvements over the years, but said it remained responsible for the building as its owner.

“The council remains responsible for the building as the owner and has continued to maintain and manage the facility while exploring its long-term future,” the statement said.

It added that ‘significant investment is required’ and warned that continuing to fund repairs to an ageing structure could become increasingly difficult.

The council said this could divert resources from a longer-term solution it believes would better serve the community.

The council said it had already undertaken a public consultation, which received responses from residents, many of whom were existing users of the sports and social club.

It said: “This feedback is helping to shape the brief for the project. Community engagement will continue as designs develop and before any final decisions are taken.”

Mr Last acknowledged the strength of feeling surrounding the building, saying the council recognised it was ‘far more than simply a bar’ and was an ‘important social venue and a valuable part of village life’.

He said the council wanted any future development to build on that heritage while providing a modern, accessible and financially sustainable facility for the future.

“The ambition is to create somewhere that local clubs and residents actively want to use and are proud to call their community hub,” he said.

#1853. Argentina star Leandro Paredes collapses during post-match interview as journalist tries to break his fall after he 'felt dizzy' at the end of the first half of Boca Juniors' cup glory

Published: 05:59 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 10:11 EST, 23 November 2026

Argentina star Leandro Paredes collapsed during a live interview immediately after winning a trophy with his Boca Juniors side.

The 32-year-old was one of the focal points of a World Cup side that reached the final last summer, and went on to win the Copa Sudamericana on Saturday evening after beating Brazil's Atletico Mineiro 2-0 in Barranquilla.

But amid the thick humidity and Colombian heat, Paredes became overwhelmed moments after lifting the trophy.

After giving a brief interview, Paredes was captured closing his eyes, before falling towards the interviewer, who attempted to break his fall.

Instead, the former Paris Saint-Germain midfielder hit the ground, with attendants rushing to help him after his collapse.

Paredes had been taken off in the second-half after suffering from heat-related dizziness, with humidity at 80 per cent heading into the match, and 32-degree-temperatures.

Leandro Parades collapsed to the floor during a post-match interview after winning the Copa Sudamericana with Boca Juniors

The interviewer attempted to break his fall as the former PSG crumpled to the turf

'He felt dizzy towards the end of the first-half,' his manager Rodolfo Arruabarrena explained of the substitution. 'He improved a little during the break, but after 10 minutes in the second-half, you could see he was struggling.'

Fortunately, Paredes was revived quickly and treated in the treatment room, before re-joining his team's celebrations after claiming the South American trophy.

The star shared a brief statement on social media confirming he was fine after the interview aired.

'We're fine,' Paredes confirmed with a picture taken during treatment, before adding in a separate caption: 'Thanks to everyone for the messages, it was just a dizziness from so many turns together'.

Paredes' triumph for his club side comes months after agonising defeat to Spain in New York at the World Cup final in July.

Argentina were felled by a solitary goal from Ferran Torres to end their reign as world champions, before the match descended into petty scraps - with Paredes at the heart of the bad behaviour.

Paredes furiously shoved Spain substitute Gavi to the floor after the final whistle blew, earning himself a punchy 10-match suspension from FIFA.

He faced three assault charges, while teammate Nahuel Molina faced two, and both players were also fined $90,000 (£66,000).

Paredes himself admitted that the length of the ban had put his international future under consideration.

'It's going to be difficult for me to stay with the national team,' Paredes told the media in September. 'Because of the suspension as well, because of (Lionel Messi) Leo's decision. It's going to be difficult for everything to carry on as before.

'I haven't discussed it with the coach (Lionel Scaloni) yet, but we'll talk about it and see what decision I make.'

Paredes' announcement came just days after Messi decided to hang up his international boots, with the talismanic Argentina superstar treated to a magnificent send-off during the early Autumn international break.

'Leo's legacy will live on forever because of what he achieved, for never giving up and for showing that dreams are hard-won, pursued and, in the end, fulfilled,' Paredes added.

Paredes updated fans after the incident to confirm he was okay before rejoining the festivities with his team-mates (Source: Instagram/Leandro Parades)

'We'd spoken in the final days of the World Cup about how the final would surely be his last match, but even so, we weren't prepared for that because of what he means to us.'

Although unable to compete alongside him in their country's colours for one last time, Paredes joined Messi on the pitch in Buenos Aires for his final farewell, and shared an emotional tribute post to his former captain.

'THANK YOU FOR ABSOLUTELY EVERYTHING CAPTAIN,' he captioned a carousel of photos of himself and Messi.

'It was a dream to be able to have achieved everything we achieved together and to have defended this shirt and our country with you, I'm leaving and we'll miss you always.

'It was a pleasure to be one of your soldiers for all these years and I will be forever! I love you buddy.'

#1852. Real Salt Lake vs Vancouver Whitecaps - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 25 Nov 2026 14:36

Real Salt Lake will try to extend their season into next week with a Friday win over the Vancouver Whitecaps at America First Field in game two of that best-of-three playoff series.

The reigning MLS Cup runners-up captured game one 2-0 last Sunday, putting them one win away from round two in the Western Conference playoffs.

After surviving a nervy shootout in the Wild Card Round, Salt Lake are now on the brink of elimination yet again after a subpar showing in game one against the Caps.

On Sunday, Pablo Mastroeni’s men suffered just their second defeat in their last eight MLS outings and were second-best for much of the game.

While they are on the verge of another early exit, they can draw optimism from being unbeaten in their last four MLS affairs at America First Field.

During the regular season, Salt Lake showed strong attacking potency on home soil, netting three or more goals six times and scoring multiple times on 12 separate occasions.

They will try to end a five-match playoff losing run on Friday, scoring a goal or fewer in each of those instances.

Claret and Cobalt have not lost a playoff match at home in 90 minutes this decade, with their only such victory at America First Field occurring on penalties versus the Houston Dynamo in game two of that opening round series.

#1851. Amorim explains dislike for ‘AmorimBall’ term and what leaves him ‘really worried’ about Milan

Ruben Amorim had some interesting comments after the Frosinone win, including why he is not a fan of a term that is going viral.

Milan put on a five-star display at San Siro on Sunday night as they routed that Canarini. All five of their goals came via flowing counter-attacks, which has led to the tag ‘AmorimBall’ doing the rounds on social media, with many believing things are starting to truly click.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The head coach is keeping his feet firmly on the ground though, as he spoke after the game about the need to find consistency both within matches but also from game-to-game. In this sense, Thursday’s trip to face Olympiacos is another big test.

Amorim was present in the press conference room at San Siro following the win to answer questions from journalists, with his comments relayed by MilanNews.

“I don’t like that expression. I think we play games to win, we want to dominate the opponent. I don’t think we succeeded today: every game has its own story, and today it was man-on-man.

“Today we didn’t have to prepare much: the idea was simply to give the ball to Pulisic, to Moreira, and then exploit the combinations of these players, the understandings they already have, and conquer space.

“Today you saw that we didn’t spend much time near the opponent’s penalty area and we scored five goals, because the space wasn’t there, it was forty meters away to attack on the run.

“That’s why Cisse came on to play as a striker and not, for example, Camarda: because there was space behind him and Cisse is very good at that. So, I think we’ve played very good games in the past, but today it was just a question of the quality of the players, of one-on-ones, of reading the game.

“Today it wasn’t a question of the coach, I think, but of the players. And they, since it was man-on-man, just had to do what they can do. when they’re so good: beating the man and opening up space. So today the credit goes entirely to the players.”

“I watched the France game and I think he’s one of the best players on the team. So I think his importance is paramount. You can see there’s rotation, there’s a lot of talent. France has a lot of talent, but Rabiot is always there. There’s a reason for that.

“And then, if you look at the way France play, with Mbappé, with the way all these players position themselves on the pitch, sometimes with four players with Olise as the No. 10, he has to stay there to play a different kind of game.

“With us, he’s the player who has to push the team forward, he’s the decisive element. In France, however, he has a different job to do. So it depends more on his role in the national team and his role at Milan.

“This changes his way of interpreting the game, and it’s further proof of how Rabiot can play by adapting to the team he’s in. For me, therefore, he’s one of the best midfielders in Europe. I hope his contract renewal comes soon.”

“Today’s match wasn’t just about tactics. We saw changes in position, one-on-one situations with plenty of space: it seemed like a crazy game. What I felt against Genoa and in the other matches was that we were too far away, we didn’t reach the final third of the pitch.

“We’re not like the big teams: if you look at the big teams, like Juventus, they might struggle to get results, but you see the volume they produce. For us, it’s a bit of the opposite, so I’m really worried that, if we don’t improve, we won’t be able to maintain this number of points.

“Today, however, was a step forward: we saw many players attacking the depth, something we hadn’t seen against Ferencvaros. In the other matches, we’d managed the ball well, but today we needed pace and runs.

“We need to be able to play both games within the same game, but today was clearly the type of game we needed to win.”

#1848. 'As late as my postman' - Brighton's European drama explained as VAR intervenes

Universitatea Craiova defender Vladimir Screciu was sent off for standing on Matt O'Riley's ankle, at the Amex Stadium, on Thursday night (November 26).

The Romanian league leaders found themselves down to ten men in the 39th minute, with referee Matthias Jöllenbeck showing Screciu a red card as the first half approached its conclusion.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Screciu caught O'Riley on the foot, leaving the Brighton midfielder requiring lengthy treatment.

However, the incident initially went unnoticed by the referee, with play continuing on the other side of the pitch.

It was only after the officials became aware of the incident that the game was stopped and the decision reviewed by VAR.

Warren Aspinall, former Brighton striker on BBC Sussex, said: “Vladimir Screciu's as late as my postman. He's off.

“He's had a bad time, the second goal and now he's been sent off. I thought Matt O'Riley had just rolled it.”

A stretcher was ready pitch-side but O'Riley was thankfully able to return to the pitch after receiving treatment.

The dismissal came with Brighton already holding a 2-0 lead, putting Fabian Hürzeler's side in a commanding position in their fourth Conference League league-phase fixture.

Ibrahim Osman had given Albion the perfect start, finding the net in the third minute after being set up by Jack Hinshelwood.

Maxim De Cuyper then doubled the advantage in the 33rd minute, leaving Craiova with a difficult task even before they lost one of their players.

What does the red card mean for Brighton?

For Hürzeler, the sending-off offered an opportunity to take greater control of proceedings.

With an extra player on the pitch, Brighton can look to stretch Craiova, move the ball across the pitch and exploit the spaces left by a side forced to defend with fewer players.

It also presents a chance to manage the game intelligently, particularly with a busy domestic schedule approaching.

Aspinall said: “It's too easy, when they had 11 on and now it's worse. Craiova haven't offered anything; they're slow. They've played five at the back and we cut them open after three minutes.

“I'd bring Lewis Dunk on, he could be like Tom Brady out there. They need the ball quicker; Pascal Struijk needs to do the same. They kept hitting the ball so hard it wasn't going to anybody.

“Start showing you deserve this spot in the team, and give the manager a headache. If they don't score six or seven goals tonight, I'll be disappointed.”

Aspinall wasn’t completely convinced by the first-half showing.

"The manager is having a go at some of these players, and rightly so,” he said.

"Get your pass right and if you're playing like this against Newcastle on Sunday, they'll be in trouble.”

Hürzeler made three changes at half-time, introducing Femi Azeez, Yasin Ayari and Costinha.

It was a particularly notable moment for Azeez, who made his Brighton debut after coming on as part of the triple substitution.

O'Riley, De Cuyper and Chema Andrés were the players withdrawn, with the Seagulls looking to manage their advantage and take control of the second half.

With Craiova down to ten men and Brighton already two goals ahead, the hosts are in an excellent position to secure another important European result.

Albion had arrived at the fixture looking to respond after their 2-0 defeat away to Hull City, and a convincing European performance would provide a welcome boost.

Both clubs had collected seven points from their opening three Conference League matches, making the meeting an important opportunity to strengthen their position in the league phase.

#1845. No advantage played and an indirect free-kick: Pairetto criticised for Milan-Frosinone officiating

Referee Luca Pairetto has been criticised for his performance in AC Milan’s 5-1 win over Frosinone last night.

This morning’s edition of La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) comments on three incidents above all in which the referee ultimately seemed incapable of providing the right decision, one of which could have cost a goal.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In the first half, Adrien Rabiot stole the ball from Cittadini, who blatantly dragged him back by the shirt. The ball rolled to Goncalo Ramos who was through on goal and had a man to his left, effectively making it a two-on-zero break with just the goalkeeper to beat.

Yet, the referee Pairetto blew his whistle for a foul and showed a yellow card to the defender. He immediately apologised for his error in failing to play the clear advantage for the Rossoneri, in an incident reminiscent of the Junior Messias goal not given against Spezia in 2021-22.

That wasn’t all, either. Nine minutes into the second half, an indirect free-kick was awarded inside the Frosinone penalty area following a clear back-pass from Calvani to Palmisani, that was actually flagged by the assistant referee and not initially given by Pairetto.

Former referee Mauro Bergonzi commented on the refereeing incidents in Milan-Frosinone to La Domenica Sportiva.

“In the first half, the referee failed to take the lead: he missed the lead, he squandered it, if we’re being honest. The situation is this: Cittadini fouls Rabiot, who steals the ball, a clear hold, the referee hastily calls the foul, and he also realises it immediately because he stops, as if to say, ‘Wow, it’s a shame I called’ because Gonçalo Ramos was hurtling toward goal.

“He apologizes, he says: ‘No, I apologise, I’m booking the Frosinone player.’ He said sorry. But this is something that really bothers you from a refereeing perspective because the lead was clear, but the referee’s gesture is commendable because he raises his hands and humbly says: ‘I made a mistake’.

“53rd minute: we rarely see them called on football pitches during matches. It’s a deliberate back pass from Calvani to the goalkeeper, the goalkeeper saves it, the referee wouldn’t have called anything, he turns to the right, looks at the assistant because the assistant signals it to him.

“Pairetto tells the assistant, ‘Well done’ and, to make matters worse, ‘Well done’ again. The assistant was good because he saw it perfectly correctly. He made his choice, he got it right because this is a pass, a deliberate back pass.

“Chiffi, the fourth official, is also there, pressing the button to communicate with the refereeing team via his headset, and if the assistant hadn’t seen it, the fourth official would have signaled it.”

#1844. Maritimo vs Nacional - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 25 Nov 2026 16:48

Maritimo and Nacional renew their Madeira derby rivalry in the Primeira Liga on Friday evening, with both sides looking to claim an important victory and move further clear of the drop zone.

The two clubs are meeting in the top flight for the first time in five years, with the visitors sitting 13th in the Primeira Liga table on 10 points from 11 matches, just two points above the 15th-placed hosts, who have a game in hand against Estoril Praia and sit outside the relegation playoff place on head-to-head points ahead of Casa Pia.

Maritimo made an encouraging start to life back in the top flight, winning their opening two league fixtures against Casa Pia and Famalicao, but they have not claimed another Primeira Liga victory since beating the latter on August 16.

Mitchell van der Gaag's side have since gone eight league matches without a win (D2, L6), including defeats in their last three such outings against Porto (2-1), Vitoria de Guimaraes (5-0) and Santa Clara (2-0).

Only bottom-placed Estoril, who are yet to win a league match this season, have endured a longer winless run, while Maritimo have scored the third-fewest goals in the division (nine) and conceded the third-most (21).

Van der Gaag's men have also struggled to make home advantage count, recording just one victory from five league matches at their own ground and losing the last three, during which they conceded multiple goals on each occasion and scored just once.

Maritimo did, however, receive a welcome boost in the Taca de Portugal last weekend, progressing past Chaves following a goalless draw and a 3-2 penalty shootout victory, and will hope that result provides some momentum ahead of Friday's derby.

Nacional have also endured a difficult start to the campaign, but they have collected six points from their last three matches, including a 1-0 victory over Academico de Viseu courtesy of Matchoi Djalo's late winner.

That result marked the first victory under new boss Joao Henriques, who arrived in late October as the club's third permanent manager of the season following the departures of Joao Giao and Alexandre Santos.

Henriques initially struggled to build on interim coach Bruno Abreu's home victory over Braga, losing away to Arouca in his first match in charge, but the latest success has given the Alvinegros an opportunity to record consecutive competitive wins for the first time since beating Alverca and Tondela in April.

Interestingly, Nacional's last four matches have each produced just one goal, including their disappointing Taca de Portugal defeat to lower-division Sanjoanense on October 17, meaning taking maximum points on Friday could hinge on greater efficiency in attack and defensive discipline.

However, the Islanders still have plenty of room for improvement away from home, having collected just one point from five Primeira Liga trips this season, drawing at Santa Clara on the opening weekend before losing their next four against Vitoria, Sporting, Rio Ave and Arouca.

Nacional have also found this fixture difficult in recent meetings, losing four of their last five league encounters with Maritimo across the Primeira Liga and Liga 2 (D1), including a 3-1 defeat on their most recent competitive visit.

Maritimo are monitoring defenders Rafael Fernandes (muscle) and Paulo Henrique (thigh), who both missed last weekend's cup tie against Chaves.

Yellu Santiago is also working his way back to full fitness from an injury, having only featured in the opening weekend of the Primeira Liga campaign.

Goncal Tabuaco's performance against Chaves has given Van der Gaag a decision to make in goal after he replaced Fran Vieites in the cup, saving two penalties during the shootout.

Nacional will be without Ulisses Wilson and Filipe Soares, who are both recovering from ankle injuries and remain unavailable.

Leo Santos (knee) is also sidelined, while Brazilian duo Wesley Gasolina and Liziero continue to recover from their respective injuries.

Henriques could retain the lineup that started against Viseu, with Miguel Baeza anchoring the midfield, although Djalo is pushing for a starting place after making an impact from the bench last time out.

#1843. OLIVER HOLT: Man United ARE in a relegation battle - anybody who denies it is deluding themselves - and Mauricio Pochettino is already showing signs of cracking under pressure

Published: 07:54 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:31 EST, 23 November 2026

Early on in On the Road, somewhere between Chicago and Denver, Jack Kerouac described the journey his main character was taking and some of the trepidation that came with each new horizon. ‘I was halfway across America,’ he wrote, ‘at the dividing line between the East of my youth and the West of my future.’

Late on Sunday afternoon, as winter’s grey light turned to darkness on Merseyside and a bitter wind blew in off the Irish Sea, Manchester United’s new boss, Mauricio Pochettino, freshly arrived from Cincinnati, Ohio, arms folded grimly and tightly across his chest, stood on the touchline at Anfield and realised the full extent of what he had just got himself into.

Sure, the United job was too big to turn down. However far the club has fallen, it still has that lure. It still has the name, even if the name is now just one of those building facades on a film set.

There is the name and then there is the nothingness that is concealed beyond the name. There is the mismanaged, mistreated void that United has become.

And now United need to find out which version of Pochettino they have purchased. Because he is at a dividing line, too. Do they have the Pochettino who blazed a trail across the football landscape with Espanyol, Southampton and Spurs, although he did not win trophies at any of those destinations?

Or do they have the Pochettino whose reputation gradually became becalmed at Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and the USA national team? They better hope they can restart something in him because this is the biggest and the hardest job Pochettino has ever had and it will take a Herculean effort just to survive.

Do Man United have the Mauricio Pochettino who blazed a trail with Espanyol, Southampton and Spurs? Or do they have the Pochettino whose reputation has fluctuated since?

That is what this season is about now for these fallen, ruined giants. It is about survival. Nothing more. If Pochettino did not realise it before, he will have realised it during that calamitous 4-0 defeat at Anfield: United are in a relegation battle and anyone who denies that is deluding themselves.

That is just pride talking. The remnants of what pride remains at United, anyway.

Maybe it hasn’t quite seemed real until now. Just like the prospect of Leicester City winning the Premier League didn’t start to feel real until around Christmas of 2015-16. United going down would be up there with Leicester winning the title in terms of seismic events in the modern English game. It’s time to start taking relegation seriously.

If you take the blinkers off for just a second, if you banish the muscle memory that tells you United are too successful and too rich to get sucked down into the Championship, then you have to accept that all the ingredients are there for United to get relegated. Take that name away and what’s left?

What’s left is a team that last won a Premier League game on August 30. What’s left is a team that has won one game all season. What’s left is a team that has conceded 34 goals across all competitions, more than any other team in Europe's top five leagues. What’s left is a team that has eight points from its first 11 league games.

Just for context, the Spurs side that spent most of last season haunted by the prospect of relegation, had 18 points at this stage of that campaign. If you still think the rabble currently representing the club are too good to go down, I think you are deluding yourself.

Yes, United played more than 80 minutes of the game against Liverpool with 10 men and, yes, the decision to send off Leny Yoro for his challenge on Alexander Isak was harsh. But the dismissal was also a fig-leaf for Pochettino and United. It was convenient. It was a disguise for what lay beneath.

United also brought it on themselves. Pochettino made one big selection decision before the game when he picked Matthijs de Ligt ahead of Harry Maguire. It was what former bosses in the English game might have described as a ‘big rick’. It was a terrible misjudgment.

Maybe the sending off of Leny Yoro was harsh. But United brought it on themselves

Matthijs de Ligt (right) was bullied by Alexander Isak at Anfield. Pochettino's decision to play the Dutchman was a terrible misjudgment

De Ligt’s first action was to watch a long ball from Ronald Araujo sail over his head, gazing at it with a mix of horror and wonder, as you might if you were watching the trajectory of an alien spaceship. Yoro was not quick enough to read De Ligt’s discomfort and so the horror ensued.

It was Pochettino’s first game and it is impossible to judge him yet but it is possible to say this was a bad start.

There were even a couple of worrying signs in his post-match press conference when the bonhomie and the relaxed demeanour that are among his great strengths deserted him.

When he was asked about United being in the relegation zone, he snapped that it was a ‘cheap’ question because he had only just arrived at the club. He said he saw fight in his players, which few others had seen. He blamed everything on the sending off of Yoro, even though it was his selection of De Ligt that had led to it.

A few alarm bells started to ring. Only faintly and only in the distance but they were ringing nonetheless. Pochettino has had big jobs before but he has never had a job as big as Manchester United where the scrutiny and the expectation and the judgment is relentless and unforgiving.

Pochettino has dealt with Daniel Levy at Spurs, which may not have been an easy relationship, but he has never dealt with a clown-show like the one that Jim Ratcliffe has put in place at Old Trafford.

United is rotten. Everyone can see that. Off the pitch, the club is at war with its own fans. The club gives every impression of trying to move on its most loyal supporters so that it can replace them with tourists and day-trippers who will spend more on tickets and in the club superstore and at the food stands.

‘The way you treat us is a disgrace,’ that banner in the Stretford End said a few weeks ago, and that is how the fans feel. They are more loyal than United deserve but their patience with their owners ran out a long time ago. Pochettino has a disaffected fanbase to deal with as well.

United is rotten on the pitch and it is rotten off the pitch. It feels as if the club is being slowly poisoned in plain sight. It feels as if it is getting weaker and weaker and weaker. And when Brentford arrive at Old Trafford next week, they will smell blood. Every club that comes to Old Trafford now smells blood.

Harry Maguire looks dejected at full-time on Sunday. United is rotten on the pitch and it is rotten off the pitch. It feels as if the club is being slowly poisoned in plain sight

Still think they’re too good to go down? Who are they better than in this league? Hull City? United don’t have the spirit of Hull City. They don’t have the togetherness. They don’t have the pride.

Hull got battered by Brighton on Sunday afternoon and still won 2-0. United could never have done that. United have already lost to Hull and Brighton this season, too.

So, yes, United are in a relegation fight. They’re one off the bottom of the league in the last week of November. Of course, they’re in a relegation fight. It’s on their new boss to get them out of it.

If Pochettino is on the wrong side of the dividing line of his career, if the best part of his journey is behind him, United are in big, big trouble.
